extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and press professionals (editors/publishers), plus readers interested in national/international politics
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-article news front page (AP-style dispatches) covering domestic policy (agriculture, labor), a major public address to newspaper publishers, and United Nations Security Council proceedings. The page contains reportage plus normative guidance embedded in speeches and procedural descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper as a record of national achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: “The American newspaper, as a record of national achievements and of the counsel of much wisdom...”—the press should serve as the nation's historical record and chronicler of public affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newspapers should document national achievements and counsel; act as an authoritative record for public memory. (Context: Eisenhower's address to publishers emphasizing the press's role as chronicler and instructor.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect emotions but point out the path of logic
rubrics_metrics.description: The newspaper “must reflect the day-to-day attitude—even the emotions—of the people it serves. But equally the newspaper must strive to point out the path of logic.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance reporting of popular sentiment and emotion with analytic, logical explanation. Do not merely amplify emotion; help readers understand the reasoning and consequences behind events and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote mutual international understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through every means open to us, we must strive for comprehension of the history, the problems and the aspirations of others... the newspaper... can do more to facilitate progress along the road of mutual understanding than those who direct the publicity media.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News coverage should help readers understand foreign peoples' histories, problems and aspirations to reduce fear, suspicion and prejudice. Avoid parochial framing; encourage comprehension and tolerance via reporting choices and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide intelligent familiarity with military/security problems
rubrics_metrics.description: “Intelligent familiarity with military problems is as essential to good citizenship as is knowledge of public schools or public finance... the newspaper can bring to our people definite understanding of the immediate roles that our security forces must play...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report clearly on military and security matters to educate citizens: explain roles, capabilities, limitations and necessary preparations. Improve information services and keep the public informed of progress and problems within the security establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise the duty to criticize defects in the military establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The free press “has exercised its right and its duty to criticize defects discovered in the structure of our military establishment... That was as much a part of your essential function as your wartime effort.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative and critical reporting on military organization, discipline, and human-relations issues is an essential press responsibility; such criticism supports accountability and effective reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid belligerence and maintain democratic representation in security policy
rubrics_metrics.description: “The security establishment of our democracy must always remain representative of our way of life. It must not be a belligerent and noisy horde... It must not attempt to build the country into a warehouse stockpile for war.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage and policy should guard against militaristic posturing, undue secrecy or creation of privileged castes within the security establishment. Emphasize civilian oversight, proportionality and preservation of peaceful civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate progressive, coordinated disarmament (caution against unbalanced disarmament)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Three roads lead to peace... progressive international disarmament... unco-ordinated disarmament by itself is a treacherous road... The caution to be observed is that disarmament is not unbalanced.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing disarmament policy, prioritize gradual, multilateral and well-coordinated measures; evaluate proposals for balance and the risk that unilateral or uncoordinated cuts could produce insecurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for voluntary arbitration in industrial disputes (A.N.P.A. position)
rubrics_metrics.description: A.N.P.A. affirms its long-established policy of voluntary arbitration: “If conciliation fails in the absence of voluntary arbitration, no other machinery seems available except compulsory arbitration. ‘Compulsory arbitration is unenforceable unless fostered by Government... it can impair collective bargaining.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor disputes in the newspaper business should be resolved primarily through voluntary arbitration and conciliation; compulsory arbitration is a last resort and may bring governmental overreach and impair collective bargaining. (Context: publishers' association policy statement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: UN Security Council threshold questions for action
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering whether to investigate or act, ask: (1) Is the situation likely to endanger the maintenance of international peace and security? (2) Is the situation one which might lead to or give rise to a dispute? (Also: collect documentary evidence.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use those threshold questions to decide whether to appoint a commission or take further measures. The Council should base action on facts and documentary evidence and may appoint a fact-finding commission when warranted (context: debate over charges against Spain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to non-substantive changes to official record within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegates are given 24 hours after publication of the record to make changes not affecting the substance of their arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rule: delegate corrections to the official journal are limited to non-substantive alterations within a 24-hour window after publication; substantive changes require further process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council may appoint fact-finding commissions before substantive action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council can appoint a fact-finding commission to study charges (example: Australian proposal to appoint fact-finding commission to study the Spanish question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before taking punitive or diplomatic measures, the Council may seek a commission to gather facts; such commissions are appropriate when documentary evidence is incomplete or disputed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for government incentives to draw stored grain (policy instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an incentive to draw stored wheat from farms, the Department of Agriculture has offered a bonus (cents a bushel) on grain delivered before June 15; similar offers on corn produced immediate response—objective: move stocks toward a national goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or designing agricultural emergency measures, use targeted financial incentives and clear delivery deadlines to encourage rapid market participation and meet stockpile goals. (Context: wartime/postwar food relief logistics.)
